# Configuring Monitor and Effect Blocks in a Process Control System

The system provides a comprehensive method for configuring monitor blocks and effect blocks within a process control environment. This configuration process is facilitated through a graphical user interface (GUI) that is presented to users on a display device, enabling intuitive and efficient system setup.

## Graphical User Interface Overview

At the core of the configuration process is the graphical user interface, which visually represents the essential components of the control system. Specifically, the interface displays a first monitor block, a second monitor block, and an effect block. By rendering these blocks graphically, the system allows users to interact directly with each component, streamlining the configuration workflow and improving overall usability.

## Establishing Connections Between Monitor Blocks

Through the input device, users are able to configure the relationships between the various blocks. In particular, the system enables one of the outputs of the first monitor block to be designated as an input to the second monitor block. This capability allows the two monitor blocks to work in a coordinated manner, with the output of the first block directly influencing the operation of the second.

## Linking Monitor Blocks to the Effect Block

The system further supports the routing of signals to the effect block. An additional output from the first monitor block, along with an output from the second monitor block, can each be configured to serve as inputs to the effect block. This arrangement ensures that the effect block receives relevant information from both monitor blocks, allowing it to respond appropriately based on the combined inputs.

## Designating Trigger Cells

To capture and respond to specific plant conditions, users can designate cells within each block as triggers. Each trigger is associated with a respective input/output pair that corresponds to a particular condition within the process plant. This functionality enables the system to monitor for defined conditions and initiate the appropriate responses, thereby providing precise and reliable control over the process.

## Summary

In summary, the system offers a flexible and user-friendly approach to configuring monitor and effect blocks. By combining a graphical interface with the ability to define inter-block connections and designate condition-based triggers, the system empowers users to establish sophisticated control logic that accurately reflects the operational requirements of the process plant.

# System and Method for Configuring Monitor Blocks and Effect Blocks in a Process Control System

## Overview

The present disclosure relates to a system and method for configuring monitor blocks and effect blocks within a process control system. In modern industrial environments, process plants require sophisticated tools that allow operators and engineers to monitor plant conditions and respond appropriately to a wide range of events. The system described herein addresses these needs through an intuitive graphical user interface that simplifies the configuration process while maintaining the flexibility necessary for complex operations.

## Graphical User Interface

At the core of the system is a graphical user interface designed to display multiple monitor blocks alongside an effect block. This visual representation allows users to see, at a glance, the various components involved in the monitoring and response framework. Each monitor block is capable of receiving and evaluating specific process signals, while the effect block serves as the mechanism through which responsive actions are initiated based on the conditions detected by the monitor blocks.

The graphical interface is paired with an input device, such as a keyboard, mouse, or touchscreen, enabling users to enter configuration data directly. Through this interaction, users can define the parameters and relationships that govern how the blocks operate, all without requiring extensive programming knowledge or specialized coding expertise.

## Interconnecting Block Inputs and Outputs

One of the primary functions of the system is to allow users to interconnect the outputs and inputs of the various blocks. By linking the output of one block to the input of another, users can establish logical pathways through which information flows. This capability enables the construction of layered monitoring schemes, where the results of one evaluation may serve as the basis for subsequent evaluations or actions.

## Routing Signals to the Effect Block

In addition to interconnecting blocks, the system enables users to route signals directly to the effect block. This routing determines which conditions and inputs will influence the behavior of the effect block. When the specified conditions are met, the effect block can initiate a corresponding response, such as triggering an alarm, adjusting a process variable, or notifying an operator. The ability to precisely control signal routing gives users significant flexibility in defining how the system responds to different scenarios.

## Designating Trigger Cells

A further feature of the system is the ability to designate specific cells as triggers that correspond to particular process plant conditions. By identifying these trigger cells, users can associate distinct plant states—such as pressure thresholds, temperature limits, or equipment status changes—with defined responses. This granular level of configuration ensures that the system reacts appropriately to the specific circumstances arising within the plant.

## Advantages and Applications

Taken together, these capabilities provide a flexible and powerful framework for monitoring and responding to events within a process plant. The graphical, block-based approach reduces the complexity typically associated with configuring monitoring and response logic, making the system accessible to a broader range of users. At the same time, the interconnection, routing, and triggering features offer the depth and adaptability required to address the diverse and evolving needs of industrial process control.

By combining an intuitive user interface with robust configuration options, the system enhances both the efficiency and reliability of process monitoring, ultimately supporting safer and more effective plant operations.

# Patent Abstract

## System and Method for Configuring Monitor Blocks and Effect Blocks in a Process Control System via Graphical User Interface

A system and method for configuring interconnected functional blocks within a process control environment through a graphical user interface (GUI). The system enables users to instantiate and configure monitor blocks, which are adapted to observe process conditions and generate output signals, and effect blocks, which are adapted to execute control actions in response to received input signals. The GUI presents the monitor blocks and effect blocks as graphical elements, allowing a user to establish logical relationships by graphically connecting one or more outputs of a block to one or more inputs of another block.

The system further comprises a matrix or grid interface having a plurality of cells arranged in rows and columns, wherein individual cells may be selectively designated by a user as trigger cells. Each trigger cell defines a causal relationship such that a specified condition detected by a monitor block initiates a corresponding action performed by an associated effect block. Upon designation, the system automatically generates the underlying configuration data and control logic necessary to implement the defined interconnections and trigger relationships within the process control system.

The disclosed system reduces configuration complexity and programming errors by abstracting low-level control logic into an intuitive graphical representation, thereby enabling operators to define, visualize, and modify cause-and-effect control strategies without requiring manual coding. The resulting configuration is deployable to one or more controllers within the process control system for runtime execution.

# SYSTEM AND METHOD FOR CONFIGURING MONITOR BLOCKS AND EFFECT BLOCKS IN A PROCESS CONTROL ENVIRONMENT

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001] The present invention relates generally to process control systems, and more particularly to a system and method for configuring monitor blocks and effect blocks associated with the monitoring and control of one or more processes, wherein a graphical user interface facilitates the input and organization of configuration data by a user.

## BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

[0002] Process control systems, such as those used in chemical, petroleum, pharmaceutical, and other manufacturing processes, typically include one or more centralized or distributed controllers communicatively coupled to at least one host or operator workstation and to one or more field devices via analog, digital, or combined analog/digital communication buses or networks.

[0003] Field devices, which may include, for example, valves, valve positioners, switches, transmitters, and sensors, perform functions within the process such as opening or closing valves and measuring process parameters. The controllers receive signals indicative of process measurements made by the field devices, process this information to implement a control routine, and generate control signals that are sent over the buses or other communication lines to the field devices to control the operation of the process.

[0004] Within such systems, it is frequently desirable to monitor certain process conditions and to initiate one or more responsive actions when a monitored condition satisfies a predetermined criterion. However, configuring the logical relationships between monitored conditions and responsive actions has historically required substantial programming expertise, rendering the configuration process cumbersome, error-prone, and time-consuming. A need therefore exists for an improved system and method that simplifies the configuration of monitoring and responsive control logic through an intuitive graphical interface.

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

[0005] In accordance with one aspect of the present invention, a system is provided for configuring process control logic, the system comprising a processor, a display device, and a memory storing instructions that, when executed by the processor, cause the system to display a graphical user interface enabling a user to define and configure one or more monitor blocks and one or more effect blocks, and to establish logical associations therebetween.

[0006] As used herein, a "monitor block" refers to a configurable logic element that receives one or more process inputs and evaluates the one or more process inputs against one or more user-defined conditions to produce a monitor output indicative of whether the one or more conditions are satisfied. An "effect block" refers to a configurable logic element that, in response to a monitor output or a combination of monitor outputs, initiates one or more responsive actions with respect to the process, including without limitation actuating a field device, generating an alarm, modifying a setpoint, or invoking a control routine.

[0007] In accordance with another aspect, a method is provided comprising displaying a graphical interface, receiving user input defining one or more monitor blocks, receiving user input defining one or more effect blocks, receiving user input associating the one or more monitor blocks with the one or more effect blocks, and storing configuration data representative of the monitor blocks, the effect blocks, and the associations therebetween for subsequent execution by the process control system.

## BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS

[0008] FIG. 1 is a schematic block diagram of a process control system in which the present invention may be implemented.

[0009] FIG. 2 is a representation of a graphical user interface for configuring monitor blocks and effect blocks in accordance with an embodiment of the invention.

[0010] FIG. 3 is a flowchart depicting a method for configuring monitor blocks and effect blocks in accordance with an embodiment of the invention.

[0011] FIG. 4 is a schematic representation of logical associations established between a plurality of monitor blocks and a plurality of effect blocks.

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE PREFERRED EMBODIMENTS

[0012] Referring now to FIG. 1, a process control system 10 includes one or more controllers 12 communicatively coupled to one or more field devices 14 via one or more communication buses or networks 16, and further coupled to one or more workstations 18 via a network 20. The workstation 18 includes a processor 22, a memory 24, a display device 26, and one or more user input devices 28, such as a keyboard, a pointing device, or a touch-sensitive screen.

[0013] The memory 24 stores a configuration application 30 that, when executed by the processor 22, generates and displays on the display device 26 a graphical user interface 32 through which a user may configure one or more monitor blocks 34 and one or more effect blocks 36. Upon completion of the configuration, the configuration application 30 stores configuration data in a database 38 and may download all or a portion of the configuration data to the one or more controllers 12 for execution during operation of the process.

[0014] Referring to FIG. 2, the graphical user interface 32 presents to the user a configuration workspace 40 within which representations of monitor blocks and effect blocks may be created, positioned, and interconnected. In one embodiment, the graphical user interface 32 includes a first region 42 displaying a palette of available monitor block types and effect block types, and a second region 44 comprising the workspace within which selected blocks are instantiated and configured.

[0015] To configure a monitor block, the user selects a monitor block type from the palette and positions a corresponding graphical representation within the workspace. The graphical user interface 32 thereafter presents one or more configuration fields enabling the user to input configuration data associated with the monitor block, the configuration data including, by way of example and not limitation: an identification of one or more process inputs to be monitored; one or more threshold values or reference conditions; one or more logical or comparison operators defining the condition to be evaluated; and one or more parameters governing the timing, hysteresis, or persistence of the evaluation.

[0016] To configure an effect block, the user similarly selects an effect block type from the palette and positions a corresponding graphical representation within the workspace. The graphical user interface 32 thereafter presents one or more configuration fields enabling the user to input configuration data associated with the effect block, the configuration data including, by way of example and not limitation: an identification of one or more field devices or control elements to be acted upon; a specification of the responsive action to be initiated; one or more values or setpoints to be applied; and one or more parameters governing the timing or sequencing of the responsive action.

[0017] In accordance with a further aspect of the invention, the graphical user interface 32 enables the user to establish one or more logical associations between the one or more monitor blocks and the one or more effect blocks. In one embodiment, such associations are established by graphically connecting an output of a monitor block to an input of an effect block, for example by drawing a connecting line therebetween using a pointing device. In another embodiment, associations may be established through the specification of logical expressions relating a plurality of monitor outputs to one or more effect blocks, whereby a given effect block may be configured to initiate its responsive action in response to a logical combination, such as an AND, OR, or NOT combination, of a plurality of monitor outputs.

[0018] Referring to FIG. 3, a method 100 of configuring monitor blocks and effect blocks in accordance with an embodiment of the invention is described. At step 102, the graphical user interface is displayed on the display device. At step 104, the system receives user input selecting and defining one or more monitor blocks, and at step 106, the system receives user input specifying configuration data for each such monitor block. At step 108, the system receives user input selecting and defining one or more effect blocks, and at step 110, the system receives user input specifying configuration data for each such effect block.

[0019] At step 112, the system receives user input establishing one or more logical associations between the one or more monitor blocks and the one or more effect blocks. At step 114, the system validates the configuration data and the established associations to verify consistency and completeness, and may generate an error indication or a warning to the user upon detection of an inconsistency or incompleteness. At step 116, the system stores the configuration data, representative of the monitor blocks, the effect blocks, and the associations therebetween, in a database or other memory. At step 118, the system optionally downloads all or a portion of the stored configuration data to one or more controllers for execution.

[0020] Referring to FIG. 4, an exemplary configuration is depicted wherein a plurality of monitor blocks 34a, 34b, and 34c are logically associated with a plurality of effect blocks 36a and 36b. As illustrated, the monitor output of monitor block 34a and the monitor output of monitor block 34b are combined at a logic element 46 such that effect block 36a initiates its responsive action only when the conditions of both monitor block 34a and monitor block 34b are satisfied. The monitor output of monitor block 34c is associated directly with effect block 36b, such that effect block 36b initiates its responsive action when the condition of monitor block 34c is satisfied.

[0021] During operation of the process control system, the configured monitor blocks continuously or periodically evaluate their respective process inputs against their respective conditions and generate corresponding monitor outputs. The configured effect blocks, in response to the monitor outputs and the established logical associations, selectively initiate their respective responsive actions, thereby effecting monitoring and control of the process in accordance with the user-defined configuration.

[0022] It will be understood that the monitor blocks and effect blocks described herein may be implemented as software objects, function blocks, or other modular logic constructs, and may be executed within the one or more controllers, within the workstation, within the field devices, or in any combination thereof, without departing from the scope of the invention.

[0023] While the foregoing description sets forth particular embodiments of the invention, numerous modifications, variations, and alternative implementations will be apparent to those of ordinary skill in the art. Accordingly, the foregoing description is intended to be illustrative rather than limiting, and the scope of the invention is defined by the appended claims and their equivalents.

   receiving, via the graphical user interface, user input defining one or more effect blocks, each effect block configured to initiate a responsive action with respect to a process;
   receiving, via the graphical user interface, user input establishing one or more logical associations between the one or more monitor blocks and the one or more effect blocks; and
   storing configuration data representative of the one or more monitor blocks, the one or more effect blocks, and the one or more logical associations therebetween.

2. The method of claim 1, further comprising downloading at least a portion of the stored configuration data to one or more controllers of a process control system for execution.

3. The method of claim 1, wherein establishing the one or more logical associations comprises graphically connecting an output of a monitor block to an input of an effect block within a workspace of the graphical user interface.

4. The method of claim 1, wherein at least one effect block is configured to initiate its responsive action in response to a logical combination of a plurality of monitor outputs.

5. The method of claim 1, further comprising validating the configuration data and generating an indication upon detection of an inconsistency or incompleteness therein.

6. A system for configuring process control logic, comprising:

8. The system of claim 6, wherein each monitor block is configured to receive an identification of one or more process inputs, one or more reference conditions, and one or more comparison operators.
